body.x: Human Fitness Lab Co., Ltd. (CEO JEE YUN SUNG) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Human Fitness Lab is a business that has used their in-depth understanding of culture and arts to study and develop athletic solutions that are painless, stress-free, and fun. Through their efforts, the startup succeeded in developing the Sports DGX solution based on percussion performance. Sports DGX has been highly anticipated since its launch, achieving 2,005% of the original funding target on the domestic crowd funding platform wadiz.

Sports DGX is an at-home workout solution developed for the Danbi K-CT project supported by the Korea Creative Content Agency from 2015 to 2016. It is inspired by the iconic non-verbal musical “Fantastik,” which has been performed for 12 years, featuring the athletic and entertaining effects inherent in percussion performance.

The solution is also equipped with technical features that highly distinguish it from other products. The fitness drum pad allows users to obtain their physical data such as calorie consumption and muscular usage through the fitness e-book, and this data is matched with the database for quantification.

Furthermore, it supports sound output via Bluetooth transmission and reception. The offering can also match musical digital data and biometrics, which can then be used to analyze the user's state and physical changes over time. Moreover, interworking is supported with a dedicated application (app) to monitor quantitative data.

According to a representative from Human Fitness Lab, “We have previously signed an agreement with a U.S. company that produces VR footages and virtual content to co-produce educational videos. In this year's CES, we plan to have meetings with buyers in regard to additional fitness distribution and investment.”

“We are going to promote the sales of at-home workout Nanta drum products and the opening of our programs through fitness centers. We'll also conduct a shared gym business in parallel to facilitate product promotion across South. Korea.” The representative added, “We are working hard to boost sales by expanding sales routes to home shopping channels and the shopping mall run by the Public Procurement Service of Korea.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
